newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's national parliament overturns euthanasia law.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's national parliament overturns euthanasia law.

text.p: The Australian parliament voted on Monday to overturn a world-first voluntary euthanasia law only nine months after it came into operation in the outback Northern Territory.
Parliament's upper house Senate voted by 38 votes to 33 in favour of a backbencher's bill, already passed by the lower house of parliament, invoking a federal right to quash territory laws.

Four people have committed assisted suicide under the Territory's Rights of the Terminally Ill Act law since it came into operation last July and at least two others have fulfilled the legal requirements to do so and are preparing to die.

The doctor who has helped all four die using a computer-delivered lethal injection, Philip Nitschke, was in the public gallery on Monday night to hear the Senate's tortuous debate, held back by procedural wrangling and failed amendments.

In quashing the law, federal parliament has both rejected the views of the 75 percent of Australians who back euthanasia and taken the constitutionally extraordinary step of overriding the laws of the self-governing Northern Territory.
The law had been condemned by a wide coalition of church and civic groups as well as by Aboriginal leaders who feared sick Aboriginals would avoid medical treatment if the law remained.
